basis: Congenital laryngeal collapse; cleft palate and cleft lip are annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting oral structural involvement.
Benign digestive tract neoplasm umbrella; hepatobiliary origins apply to particular subtypes rather than most patients.
Calvarial sclerosis, reduced bone density and fractures define the disorder; hearing impairment is very rare and dental involvement has no established frequency.
Skin defects, ankyloblepharon and oral clefts define AEC; conductive hearing loss occurs in 80-99%. Choanal atresia omitted at the four-axis cap.
Glycosylation disorder; brain atrophy/seizures and hepatic dysfunction in 80-99%; cardiac septal defects in 2/3. Renal and skeletal abnormalities omitted at cap.
Active microbial infection of a reproductive sac; the infection mechanism has an axis although the anatomical site does not.
Isolated spermatogenic failure affects reproductive function; elevated FSH reflects impaired spermatogenesis without establishing a separate endocrine disorder.
Inherited pyruvate metabolism abnormality expressed in erythrocytes, with increased red-cell ATP and polycythemia.
Combined adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; mineralocorticoid-mediated hypertension occurs in approximately 80-90% and is a defining manifestation.
Growth restriction and limb asymmetry define SRS; recurrent hypoglycemia and insulin resistance occur in 30-79%. Motor delay alone does not establish neural damage.
Usher syndrome defines retinal and hearing impairment; truncal ataxia, hyperreflexia and motor developmental delay are reported in 3/3 patients.
Inherited bile-salt transport disorder causing progressive intrahepatic cholestasis; definition explicitly states no extrahepatic features.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with common cortical malformation; hip dysplasia and ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Adrenal medullary endocrine tumour; catecholamine-mediated hypertension occurs in approximately 80-90%. Cardiomyopathy is a minority complication.
Inherited retinopathy directly affects retinal function; neurological ancestry does not establish extraocular nervous-system disease.
Carcinoma originates in sphenoid sinus respiratory mucosa; sinus location belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Recurrent painful dermal ecchymoses with autoimmune classification; coagulation abnormalities are occasional, so no haematologic axis is added.
Hereditary corticospinal degeneration defines this umbrella; additional organ involvement varies across subtypes.
Multiple bony exostoses and spastic tetraparesis are the two defining manifestations.
Retinal dystrophy with visual dysfunction and staphyloma; isolated short stature or truncal obesity in 1/3 does not establish another damaged organ.
Primary antibody deficiency; neutropenia reported in 1/1 patient supports blood-cell involvement. Respiratory infections alone do not establish chronic pulmonary damage.
Primary bone sarcoma with chondroblastic differentiation; no common additional organ damage is established.
Malignancy originates in the submandibular salivary gland, included in the gastrointestinal axis.
Teratoma originates in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the thirteen axes.
Spastic ataxia is neurological; supranuclear gaze palsy and dysphagia reflect neural dysfunction without establishing primary eye or gastrointestinal damage.
